analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. The change is documentation: a revised description of sample_age_ms (age is measured since the newest observation at snapshot time, even when an older completed observation arrives later) and a new paragraph (head lines 580-586) saying the Swift producer applies the same age rule independently to each workload bucket and current-posture series in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.observe. It states that wire fields are unchanged and that completed samples keep the receipt-order EWMA and sample counts. No code, wire shape, authorization, attestation, encryption, or trust-boundary behavior is changed, so no threat-model control (TB-002, TB-011, T-041, A-001, A-016) is weakened.

I also read the surrounding unchanged text in the three units (head lines 583-1458). It covers capacity heartbeat fields, service_reservation_released, inference_error sanitization, models_replace, prefix_cache v2 receipts, App Attest protocol 3 and autopilot. I found nothing that invalidates a threat-model assumption. The freshness text says old heartbeats cannot refresh old samples, which is consistent with availability-oriented capacity hygiene. Capacity fields are transient diagnostics and contain no prompt text, token IDs or cache keys. The coordinator-side validation and the Swift EnginePerformanceMeasurements code are outside the supplied evidence. I cannot confirm the doc matches the implementation; if it does not, that is documentation drift, not a security regression.
